# Weekly Market Briefing — October 25, 2026
*Quantitative Research | For informational purposes only — no trade recommendations*

## 1. Market Regime: Cautious, Rate-Pause Backdrop
The macro setup is a **normal, upward-sloping curve** (10Y-3M at +0.96 pts) with the **10Y at 4.99% (▼0.13% MoM)** and the **3M T-bill pinned at 4.03%**. The **VIX jumped to 19.45 (▲4.27 MoM)** — still a "normal" regime, but a clear uptick in nervousness, while **DXY firmed to 101.81 (▲0.84)**. Broad-market factor reads skew **mildly risk-off defensive**: SPY carries a strong Low-Vol rank (69) and solid Value (72), while large-cap momentum is only middling (SPY 54, QQQ 58). The Fed decision lands this Wednesday (Oct 28); markets put a ~94% chance the Fed maintains its rate, and rate-hike expectations eased this week — from roughly 17% last Friday down to about 10%.

## 2. This Week's News
It was a two-sided, risk-off-tilted week. The Nasdaq fell more than 2% Thursday for its worst day since June, as renewed concerns around AI-company spending and jumping oil prices (amid geopolitical tensions) sparked a sell-off. Friday extended the pain: the Dow dropped 652.82 points (-1.23%), the S&P 500 slipped 0.52%, and the Nasdaq lost 0.21%. On the week, the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, the Nasdaq shed 0.7%, and the Dow gained 0.4%. Notably, the S&P 500 ex-AI is up about 6.6% in October, while the AI-financing-weighed S&P 500 is down roughly 0.4% — a broadening away from mega-cap tech. Overseas, China's CSI 300 entered bear-market territory, falling 20% from its June peak.
